The source recommends surveying top customers — did the welcome kit, the material item, or the 90-day transformation program actually influence the decision? Rotate out components no one values.","Reiterate the offer, the guarantee and social proof at checkout, not just on the landing page. IM8 repeats a 90-day money-back promise for quarterly plans, three core value propositions, and a wall of reviews at checkout, a step the source notes people rarely optimize.","Track the AOV effect of the stack against actual product cost and shipping weight before scaling it."],"caveats":["Free physical items add COGS and fulfillment complexity; only viable where unit margin or subscription payback covers them.","The source describes IM8's stack as continually tweaked, so treat any specific item list as a snapshot rather than a fixed best practice."],"tags":["multi","offer-design","bundles","conversion-optimization","checkout","retention","fulfillment"]},{"title":"Match traffic stage-of-awareness to the right destination: advertorial/quiz, persona page, or PDP","summary":"Route cold traffic to education (third-party advertorial or quiz), problem/solution-aware traffic to persona-specific landing pages, and bottom-of-funnel retargeting straight to PDPs.","use_when":"Deciding where each ad or campaign in your account should point, and fixing mismatches between ad message and landing page experience.","steps":["For unaware and problem-aware traffic, send people to an education step rather than a purchase page: a third-party advertorial on a separate domain or a quiz funnel. IM8 ran ads from doctor-style and other third-party pages driving to custom URLs, not always to their own domain.","For solution-aware traffic, send people to a persona-matched landing page. A GLP-1 ad goes to a GLP-1 page ('seven reasons GLP-1 users are using IM8'); a bloating ad goes to a gut/bloating page ('six reasons the bloating comes back at 2pm'). The headline should mirror the ad's promised problem.","For bottom-of-funnel retargeting — people who have seen multiple ads and visited the site — send them straight to the core PDP or homepage to check out.","Keep congruence as the governing rule: the ad message, the landing page headline and the product all need to describe the same persona and problem.","Accept churn in the education layer. IM8 retired its quiz funnel from the main account after roughly 137 of 700 ads had pointed at it, illustrating that education funnels are tests, not permanent infrastructure.","Audit your own mix: in an IM8 sample, persona pages received roughly 150 of about 700 ads, with a meaningful slice (about 88) still going to the homepage, which the source flags as a weaker destination because it tries to serve every persona at once."],"caveats":["Third-party advertorial domains and aggressive native funnels carry platform and regulatory risk that differs from running on your own domain.","The source suggests the quiz was under-used relative to the persona strategy, not that quizzes are inherently superior; those are competing options you would test."],"tags":["multi","acquisition","landing-page","product-page","conversion-optimization","creative-strategy","funnel-design"]},{"title":"Build one winning script as a template, then vary only the persona","summary":"IM8 scales creative by writing one clock/timeline script structure and swapping persona and destination page, letting them increase output without finding a spend hack.","use_when":"Scaling ad creative volume in a supplement, wellness or other benefit-led category where you need many variants without a full creative reinvention each time.","steps":["Fix the script skeleton: symptom hook aimed at one persona, a cause reframe the viewer hasn't considered, then a day-by-day clock (day 1, day 9, day 21), and end with proof then offer, guarantee and scarcity.","At each clock checkpoint, name a specific ingredient, its dose, and the effect. Rotating through compound → payoff → compound → payoff is what makes the clock format work and keeps people watching for the next checkpoint.","Write outcomes as scenes, not claims: instead of 'improves mobility', describe dancing with grandkids or going on a hike. The source attributes both better performance and lower compliance risk to scene-writing.","Change only the persona variable when you need a new concept. IM8 runs near-identical scripts for joint pain and for menopause, swapping the language and the destination landing page, which lets them scale output quickly while keeping congruence.","Expect input volume to track spend almost linearly. The source frames this as 'each ad unit holds a certain spend' (about $2,500 per creative in that scrape), so doubling spend means roughly doubling creative output rather than finding a single winner.","Reuse a proven winning structure rather than chasing novelty: the source notes 99% of copywriters won't naturally write mechanism-before-benefit, so codify it as a rule."],"caveats":["The per-creative spend figure comes from one scrape that the author admits may under-count ads on third-party pages; treat it as illustrative, not a benchmark.","Persona-swapped scripts risk stale creative and audience fatigue over time; the clock format functions partly as a retention device, so degradation is a real risk.","Aggressive symptom hooks create platform and regulatory exposure."],"tags":["multi","creative-strategy","acquisition","copywriting","experiment-design","landing-page"]},{"title":"Map creative volume across stages of awareness instead of over-weighting product-aware","summary":"IM8 weights most creative to problem- and solution-aware audiences, with only a small share of unaware and product/most-aware, and sharpens claims as audiences get colder.","use_when":"Planning your monthly creative calendar and deciding how much budget to allocate to cold, unaware testing versus retargeting and product-aware assets.","steps":["Allocate the bulk of volume to problem-aware and solution-aware concepts, where audiences know the problem and are comparing solutions — this is where IM8 concentrated the majority of a 40-ad sample.","Keep unaware creative a small share. IM8's unaware-cluster copy gets more aggressive (e.g. symptom-led hooks about kidney failure symptoms, dark urine, swelling) because bigger pattern interrupts are needed to stop a never-seen-you audience, and the source notes this is also where regulatory exposure concentrates.","Keep the mix auditable: re-sample your own active ads periodically by awareness stage, the way the source sampled 40 ads, to catch drift into over-weighting bottom-funnel assets."],"caveats":["The stage-mix percentages come from a single 40-ad sample of one brand; treat them as a reference shape, not a target distribution.","Aggressive cold-audience claims are explicitly described as carrying regulatory risk — the source frames the range as a legal trade-off, not a recommendation.","Meta and other platform ad libraries in a scrape may under-represent older or third-party-hosted ads."],"tags":["multi","creative-strategy","acquisition","conversion-optimization","experiment-design","compliance"]},{"title":"Mirror the persona-page and trust-stack playbook, and don't over-drive the homepage","summary":"IM8's landing-page strength is persona congruency plus trust assets competitors cannot easily copy (ambassador wall, science stack) — with the homepage as a weaker paid destination.","use_when":"Prioritising your landing page roadmap: deciding whether to build persona pages, add trust assets, or keep sending paid traffic to the homepage.","steps":["Build a dedicated landing page for each winning persona or angle as soon as it proves out in ads, then drive that persona's ads only to its own page. This is the single most copyable element the source identifies for CPG brands.","Invest trust budget in things competitors cannot trivially replicate. The source argues generic reviews and trust badges are meaningless precisely because everyone has them; IM8's ambassador wall and a 'science stack' layer of unique proof are the arbitrage.","Keep CRO fundamentals tight on those pages — the source judges IM8's landing CRO as strong and worth benchmarking against, with little to critique.","Reduce homepage as a paid destination. About 88 of roughly 700 ads pointed at the IM8 homepage, which the source treats as an ongoing CRO test rather than a good default, since a homepage must serve all personas and its reported conversion rate is flattered by organic traffic.","Consider splitting any advertorial or quiz funnel by persona and pairing each with its own quiz, since the source sees the quiz as under-used relative to the persona strategy."],"caveats":["Ambassador and celebrity endorsement models may be impractical or unaffordable for most brands; the source calls this the least transferable part of the playbook.","Homepage conversion data is contaminated by organic traffic, so don't compare it directly to persona-page conversion without segmenting.","Building one distinct page and quiz per persona multiplies landing page and quiz maintenance work; the source acknowledges that as why it may be a roadmap item rather than a current practice."],"tags":["multi","landing-page","conversion-optimization","acquisition","creative-strategy","product-page","trust"]},{"title":"Choose your claims lane deliberately in regulated categories","summary":"In supplements and wellness, under-claiming loses on CAC while over-claiming invites bans and legal risk, so pick your position and accept the trade-off.","use_when":"Setting copy and creative policy for a supplement, wellness or health-adjacent store, or deciding how aggressive your hooks and claims should be.","steps":["Recognise the spectrum: the source notes that if you are not aggressive you won't convert, and if you are maximally aggressive you invite regulatory and platform consequences — every brand in the category is pressing against that line.","Keep a defined internal policy on claim language. IM8's copy includes measures like a clinical-trial comparison to leading anti-depressants for mood, which the source describes as a big claim that may still be compliant but sits near the edge.","Account for account stability in your channel plan: competitors making the wildest claims in native statics often achieve better CAC and profitability, but with ad accounts repeatedly banned and businesses that become hard to sell.","Prefer scene-based outcomes over outcome claims as a partial compliance hedge. Describing daily activities rather than promising symptom fixes reduces the legal surface while the source reports it performs better anyway.","Clean up factual inconsistencies across your ad library as a compliance hygiene task. The source found IM8 ads launched the same day claiming over 700,000 customers versus 390,000 and 516,000, inconsistent with roughly 414,000 customers in disclosed figures, plus inconsistent ingredient counts across ads."],"caveats":["The source's judgement that IM8 is 'skirting the line in a good way' is the author's opinion, not a legal clearance or a universal instruction.","Regulatory requirements vary by market and product category; consult qualified local counsel rather than copying another brand's claim posture.","The social proof and ingredient-count discrepancies may reflect sample distributions or product iteration rather than intent, but the source still treats them as compliance risk for a public company."],"tags":["multi","creative-strategy","compliance","copywriting","acquisition","trust"]},{"title":"Use partner equity/royalty deals that de-lever as revenue scales","summary":"Structure ambassador and partner deals with a high initial royalty that declines as revenue grows so the cost becomes cheaper with scale, unlike fixed fees.","use_when":"Negotiating endorsement, ambassador or creator partnership deals, or evaluating whether a high-visibility partnership is worth its cost as you scale.","steps":["Prefer a royalty or equity structure that decays as a percentage of revenue over time rather than a flat fee or flat retainer, so the partner cost shrinks as a share of the P&L if growth compounds.","Model the crossover point. IM8's ambassador and royalty line fell from 14% of the P&L in Q2 to 6.2% by July 2026, and their named partner line item fell from 11% to 3.3% — the source attributes this to equity deals over fee deals and warns it only works while growth continues to compound.","Do not over-index on mega-partnerships as a transferable tactic: the source calls IM8's celebrity ambassador model the least replicable part of the whole playbook.","If you cannot land elite partners, look for other trust assets your competitors cannot demonstrate, since the source locates arbitrage and profit specifically in evidence rivals cannot match."],"caveats":["Royalty-decline structures depend on continued growth; the source explicitly notes they work for IM8 only as long as revenue keeps compounding, otherwise the percentage stops falling.","Equity or royalty arrangements need clear accounting treatment and will show as a named P&L cost line you must track."],"tags":["multi","unit-economics","trust","retention","measurement","positioning"]},{"title":"Recognise ARR annualised from a single month","summary":"Annual recurring revenue is usually the latest month multiplied by twelve, which inflates the picture when that month happens to be exceptional.","use_when":"Interpreting your own dashboards or a competitor's or supplier's growth claims before making a scaling, inventory or investment decision.","steps":["Check the base period first. The source notes ARR is almost always the current month times twelve, chosen because a fast-growing business's latest month is its best ever.","Rebuild the number on a rolling window. After IM8's exceptional July — $20.9M revenue, 47,000 new customers, reported ARR pressing toward 9 figures within 11 months of launch — the source argues you need a longer rolling period to judge the next twelve months.","When someone quotes ARR to you, ask for the underlying monthly revenue series and any seasonality, and compare the same measure across several months before reacting."],"caveats":["Annualising from a single strong month is not necessarily dishonest; the source frames it as a reporting convention to be aware of rather than a misstatement."]],"tags":["multi","measurement","financial-analysis","unit-economics","acquisition"]},{"title":"Beware quoting two different gross margins in different documents","summary":"IM8 reports 65% gross margin in its P&L but 58% contractual gross margin in its financing agreement, which suggests a built-in buffer.","use_when":"Negotiating any financing, lending or revenue-based funding arrangement, or modelling gross margin when a lender or investor supplies their own figure.","steps":["Compare the gross margin in your reported financials with the margin used in any financing or lending contract. IM8 shows 65% in the P&L against a 58% contractual figure in the billion-dollar facility.","Treat the lower contractual figure as the conservative planning number, and consider that the gap may be a deliberate buffer for future discounting or promotional pressure so the covenant stays comfortable.","Expect aggressive discounting and offer testing to compress realised gross margin, which is the scenario a contractual buffer is usually protecting against."],"caveats":["The source describes this as worth calling out but says it wouldn't be too concerned and does not assert the reason for the gap; the buffer explanation is a hypothesis.","Contractual and accounting gross margins can differ legitimately for reasons including shipping, mix and definitions of cost of goods."],"tags":["multi","measurement","pricing","unit-economics","financial-analysis"]},{"title":"Interpret cohort retention tables honestly, especially the oldest cohort","summary":"Cohort retention data must be read with awareness that early-adopter cohorts typically retain best and that a single mature cohort is thin evidence.","use_when":"Assessing your own subscription retention curves, benchmarking against a competitor's disclosed cohorts, or judging third-party retention panels.","steps":["Separate cohorts by acquisition period and read gross profit growth over time for each, not a blended retention rate. IM8 publishes a cohort table showing customers acquired per month or quarter and gross profit growth on those customers at 6-month, 12-month and full-cohort marks.","Discount the oldest cohort's retention when comparing brands. The source argues early adopters in almost any business show phenomenal retention because they sought out a new brand, so third-party transaction data showing IM8 leading at month 20 rests on a single cohort and should be treated as questionable.","Check cohort maturity before drawing conclusions: a cohort with one month of data cannot be compared against cohorts with three months, as the source notes for IM8's newest 6-month GP-to-CAC reading.","Watch for discontinuities in acquisition that break comparability — the source notes the shift from monthly to quarterly plans and constant offer testing materially change cohort growth, making extrapolation riskier."],"caveats":["Cohort curves being roughly logarithmic makes modelling defensible; the issue is specifically young cohorts under rapid change, not cohort analysis itself.","Third-party card-transaction panels have incomplete coverage of a brand's customer base and may undercount non-card or international purchases."],"tags":["multi","retention","measurement","subscriptions","customer-research"]},{"title":"Assess volume-based creative scaling against spend, and prefer video for mechanism storytelling","summary":"IM8 increased creative output roughly in step with spend rather than relying on a spend hack, and skews heavily to video to explain mechanism and stay compliant.","use_when":"Planning creative production capacity and format mix for a category where the product mechanism is complex or the brand has compliance constraints.","steps":["Set an expected spend per creative unit and plan production capacity from it. The source describes creative volume tracking spend almost linearly, with roughly $2,500 of spend per ad unit in their scrape — so doubling spend means doubling creative, not optimising a single asset.","Prioritise video over static images when your product has a mechanism to explain. IM8's creatives are substantially skewed to video because a multivitamin offers many ingredient narratives, and video lets them articulate a unique mechanism and a transformation arc that a static can't.","Keep static images for lower-funnel or native contexts; the source notes IM8 avoids top-of-funnel statics and retired their quiz funnel, which limits their ability to run aggressive native statics.","Note the compliance dimension: the source attributes IM8's caution about aggressive static formats partly to being a publicly traded company, with video giving more room for compliant expression."],"caveats":["The source describes their own anti-static view as controversial and cites native static funnels and advertorial-style assets as effective channels, particularly for less compliance-constrained brands.","The approximate per-creative spend figure comes from a scrape that may under-count third-party ads, so it is illustrative rather than a benchmark.","A public-company compliance posture is not a universal constraint; private brands have different latitude and different risk."],"tags":["multi","creative-strategy","acquisition","copywriting","compliance","experiment-design"]},{"title":"Run offer and pricing tests continuously, not as a one-off redesign","summary":"IM8 treats landing page and offer optimisation as an ongoing monthly programme, tweaking the stack, the anchor products and the default plan repeatedly.","use_when":"Setting the cadence of pricing, offer and PDP testing on a consumables store, or deciding how often to revisit your landing page.","steps":["Schedule recurring reviews of your offer stack rather than treating landing page and pricing as seasonal projects. are testing on the page — trust assets, bonuses, plan defaults, guarantee language — and rotate one variable at a time so you can attribute results.","Benchmark yourself against a strong operator pillar by pillar (offer, CRO, creative, funnel routing) and identify where you are materially behind as your improvement queue."],"caveats":["The source's judgement that IM8's offer and CRO work is as a scaling constraint you probably don't have","summary":"IM8's ability to scale with a 6-8 month payback and only 0.5 first-order GP-to-CAC came from a $1B non-dilutive facility covering 70% of Routing solution-aware traffic directly to highly congruent, persona-specific landing pages (e.g., matching a GLP-1 ad to a GLP-1 landing page), while directing bottom-of-funnel retargeting traffic straight to core product display pages (PDPs).

Look for. The definition of IM8's projected LTV-to-CAC ratio: a 3:1 ratio based on a 36-month payback period. The primary mechanism IM8 used to increase Average Order Value (AOV) to absorb a rising CAC: shifting default checkouts from monthly to quarterly subscription plans. The details of the $1B financing facility: a non-dilutive loan that self-liquidates 70% of upfront marketing costs per cohort, repaid based on that cohort's subsequent income. The trend in the 6-month Gross Profit (GP) to CAC ratio: a steady decline from 2x down to 1.03x over the last six quarters as volume scaled.

Skip. Detailed breakdowns of ad creative scripts (e.g., the "clock/timeline" mechanism), evaluations of the specific visual elements on the landing pages, or the celebrity ambassador equity model (e.g., David Beckham).

Scope mix. Almost all core.

Volume. 15 to 20.

In this video, we're going to be breaking down everything that IMH is doing in their paid ad strategy. We're going to go into creative strategies, script tearowns, landing pages, what they're doing on brand, what their public finances actually look like because they're a publicly traded company. So, we can look at it all, and then how their acquisition model and pricing and offer strategy has changed over the course of the last 6 months, which is allowing them to continue to scale. So, firstly, let's start off with the business in case you don't know them. IM8 is the fastest growing CPG brand, I believe, ever. They are this stick right here which has a bunch of multivitamins in it. It's effectively just a multivitamin in a sache and then they have some longevity products as well. Who owns it?
